<div align="center">
    <h1>
        Zabbix Windows Update Template
    </h1>
    <h4>
        Monitoring pending Windows updates and restart requirements via Zabbix Agent
    </h4>
    <br>
</div>
<br>
<br>

<!-- *********************************************************************************************************************************** -->
<!-- *** BODY ************************************************************************************************************************** -->
<!-- *********************************************************************************************************************************** -->
## Description
This template monitors pending Microsoft Windows updates and the pending-reboot flag on Windows
hosts via Zabbix Agent. The reboot requirement is collected from the Windows registry through an
active check. Pending updates are searched through the Windows Update Agent over COM with a
passive `system.run` item; a dependent item counts the returned updates.

The update search may take several minutes when Windows Update or WSUS has not checked in recently.
The raw JSON result is retained so it is possible to review which updates were pending at the time.

## What is monitored
- **Restart requirement** - whether Windows has created the `RebootRequired` registry key.
- **Pending updates** - titles of updates reported as neither installed nor hidden by Windows Update.
- **Update count** - number of pending updates, with a warning threshold controlled by a macro.
- **Collection health** - no-data alert when the update search stops delivering results.

## Requirements
- **Zabbix 7.0 or higher**
- Windows host with **Zabbix Agent or Agent 2 version 7.0 or higher** - older agents ignore the 3-minute item timeout the update search needs
- Agent interface reachable from the server or proxy (the update search is a passive check) **and** active checks configured (`ServerActive` and `Hostname`; the reboot flag is an active check)
- Windows Update Agent or WSUS available to the host
- The agent service running as **LocalSystem** (the default) or another account that may use the Windows Update Agent over COM

## Setup
All commands are for an **elevated PowerShell** (right-click **Windows PowerShell** -> **Run as
administrator**) on the monitored Windows host. Paths are those of the official Zabbix MSI
installer; if the agent was installed elsewhere, change the path in steps 2 and 3.

Not sure which agent the host runs? This prints the service name - `Zabbix Agent 2` or `Zabbix Agent`:
```powershell
Get-Service "Zabbix Agent*"
```

### 1. Check that the update search works
```powershell
(New-Object -ComObject Microsoft.Update.Session).CreateupdateSearcher().Search('IsHidden=0 and IsInstalled=0').Updates | Select-Object Title | ConvertTo-Json
```
It takes from a few seconds to a few minutes. A JSON list of update titles - or no output at all when
nothing is pending - means the host is ready. A red error instead means the Windows Update service
cannot be reached from this account; fix that first, the template cannot work around it.

### 2. Download agent config (pick Agent or Agent 2)
Download **only one** file (`windows_update.conf`). It allows exactly the one `system.run` command
this template uses; every other remote command stays denied.

Zabbix Agent 2
```powershell
$dir = "$env:ProgramFiles\Zabbix Agent 2\zabbix_agent2.d"
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $dir | Out-Null
Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "https://git.initmax.cz/initMAX-Public/zabbix-templates/-/raw/production/free/Windows_Update_by_Zabbix_Agent/7.0/windows_update.conf" -OutFile "$dir\windows_update.conf"
```

Zabbix Agent
```powershell
$dir = "$env:ProgramFiles\Zabbix Agent\zabbix_agentd.d"
New-Item -ItemType Directory -Force -Path $dir | Out-Null
Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "https://git.initmax.cz/initMAX-Public/zabbix-templates/-/raw/production/free/Windows_Update_by_Zabbix_Agent/7.0/windows_update.conf" -OutFile "$dir\windows_update.conf"
```

The file holds a single rule:
```text
AllowKey=system.run["powershell \"(New-Object -ComObject Microsoft.Update.Session).CreateupdateSearcher().Search('IsHidden=0 and IsInstalled=0').Updates|Select-Object Title |ConvertTo-Json\""]
```
No `DenyKey` line is needed: the agent denies `system.run[*]` by itself after all configured rules.

### 3. Make sure the agent reads that directory
Zabbix Agent 2
```powershell
(Select-String -Path "$env:ProgramFiles\Zabbix Agent 2\zabbix_agent2.conf" -Pattern '^Include=').Line
```
Zabbix Agent
```powershell
(Select-String -Path "$env:ProgramFiles\Zabbix Agent\zabbix_agentd.conf" -Pattern '^Include=').Line
```
An agent installed from the official MSI already answers with a line that ends in `zabbix_agent2.d\`
(or `zabbix_agentd.d\`) - then there is nothing to do. Only if no line points at the directory from
step 2, open the agent configuration file in Notepad (as administrator) and add one line to its end:
```text
Include=C:\Program Files\Zabbix Agent 2\zabbix_agent2.d\
```

### 4. Restart agent
Stop, wait, start - and look at the last line. **Do not use `Restart-Service`**: on Windows the agent
is often started again before the old process has let go of port 10050, the new one then exits with
`bind() ... failed` in its log, the service stays **Stopped** and the command reports no error.

Zabbix Agent 2
```powershell
Stop-Service "Zabbix Agent 2"; Start-Sleep -Seconds 5; Start-Service "Zabbix Agent 2"; Get-Service "Zabbix Agent 2"
```
Zabbix Agent
```powershell
Stop-Service "Zabbix Agent"; Start-Sleep -Seconds 5; Start-Service "Zabbix Agent"; Get-Service "Zabbix Agent"
```
The `Status` column has to say `Running`.

### 5. Import template
Import [`template_windows_update_by_zabbix_agent_7.0.yaml`](./7.0/template_windows_update_by_zabbix_agent_7.0.yaml)
(**Data collection -> Templates -> Import**) and link it to the Windows host.

### 6. Test item
Open the host's item **Windows Update: Pending updates RAW**, press **Test -> Get value and test**.
The dialog then shows `[...` in **Value** and the list of update titles in **Result** (an empty value is
correct too - nothing is pending). What the other answers mean:

| Answer | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `Unknown metric system.run` (Agent 2) or `Unsupported item key.` (Agent) | the agent did not load `windows_update.conf` | repeat steps 2 to 4 |
| `Timeout while executing a shell script.` | the agent - or the server or proxy asking it - is older than 7.0 and ignores the 3-minute item timeout | upgrade to 7.0 or higher |
| `Get value from agent failed: cannot connect to ...` | the agent is not running or port 10050 is closed | step 4, then the Windows firewall |

The same texts show up as the item error in **Data collection -> Hosts -> Items** when the template is
linked before the agent is configured.

### 7. Check the result
After the first polling intervals the values show up in **Monitoring -> Latest data**, filter by
tag `component: windows update`. Review `{$WU.COUNT.WARN}` before enabling alerting, and keep
`{$WU.NODATA}` above one day - an unchanged update list is stored only once a day. For the same
reason a changed `{$WU.COUNT.WARN}` takes effect with the next stored value: when the list of pending
updates changes, or within a day at the latest.

### Macros used
| Macro | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `{$WU.COUNT.WARN}` | Number of pending updates tolerated before a warning is raised | `10` |
| `{$WU.INTERVAL}` | Interval for searching Windows Update or WSUS | `1h` |
| `{$WU.NODATA}` | Time without update-search data before the no-data warning is raised | `2d` |
| `{$WU.REBOOT.INTERVAL}` | Interval for reading the pending-reboot registry flag | `10m` |
